title: Objects, their Methods and the Dot Notation
summary: Adds methods (functions stored on objects) to object literals and to constructor functions, then links this idea back to the built-in Audio object used in the drum kit. Challenge: add a clean method to the Housekeeper constructor and call it.

concepts.heading: Methods on an object
points: A method is a function attached to an object. In an object literal, add it as a property whose value is an anonymous function, e.g. moveSuitcase: function () { ... }.
Call it with dot notation plus parentheses: bellBoy1.moveSuitcase(). Properties and methods are both reached with the dot; the parentheses are what mark a method call.
In a constructor function, define it with this.moveSuitcase = function () { ... }. Every object built with new then has that method.

concepts.heading: Challenge: clean method
points: Inside the Housekeeper constructor add this.clean = function () { alert("Cleaning in progress..."); }.
Create an object with new Housekeeper(...) and call houseKeeper1.clean(). An alert should appear.
Without the parentheses you only reference the function and nothing runs.

concepts.heading: Connecting to the Audio object
points: new Audio("file") follows the same pattern as the housekeeper constructor: the capitalised name is a constructor, the argument is stored as a property (the file location) and the object has methods.

The hidden Audio constructor can be imagined as setting a file-location property and defining a play() method, which would involve things such as checking the file exists and is audio, then using the audio hardware.
Code that uses it only needs to construct the object and call the method, which is what the drum kit does with tom1.play().
Much of DOM scripting is using properties and methods of built-in objects; occasionally you define your own.
The ideas are abstract; they get familiar through repetition and later projects.

task.name: Add a clean method to Housekeeper
task.starting_point: The Housekeeper constructor from the previous lecture.
task.goal: Housekeeper objects can clean, shown with an alert or log message.
steps: Add this.clean = function () {...} that alerts "Cleaning in progress...".
Create a new Housekeeper object with new.
Call the method with the dot and parentheses.
task.expected_result: Calling the method produces the 'Cleaning in progress...' message.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 18 - Advanced Javascript and DOM Manipulation/18.06 - Objects, their Methods and the Dot Notation/script.js

pitfalls: Assigning the method to a local variable instead of this.clean, so it is not attached to the object.
(Extra) The reference repo logs geovana.clean() inside console.log, which prints the method's own output first and then undefined because the method returns nothing; call geovana.clean() alone.
Mixing up property access (no parentheses) with method calls (parentheses).
